In the LWS inference case where each LWS replica represents a model you have no way to say give me a minimum of x models or none." There are multiple issues here, lets split them: 1) On gang scheduling semantics for LWS vs Deployment. The Workload api doesn't specify how gang scheduling is applied to a specific "deployment" api (LWS, Deployment, StatefulSet etc.), it is more about how one sets the selectors. If one sets the selectors to define a gang as pods in a Deployment, then that Deployment's pods will be gang scheduled. For cases like LWS, which defines groups of pods as replicas, then the workload api also gives the ability to define "replicated gangs". So I don't believe there is inconsistency. 2) On minCount, this is specific to gang scheduling of pods (pods specifically, not "replicas", as in not LWS replicas, only pods within the gang) that should be scheduled in an all-or-nothing manner. Management of individual replicas, whether the replica is a group of pods (in LWS case) or individual pods (in Deployment case), is a separate matter from gang scheduling. 3) On minCount and the lack of guarantees for the leader, I indeed think this is a gap, but it should be possible to amend the api to take this case into account. Great catch! 4) On managing groups of replicas (for example at least x prefill and y decode), whether a replica is a pod or a group of pods, this is not looked at as a gang-scheduling (all-or-nothing) problem per se; k8s has an API called PodDisruptionBudget (PDB), admittedly the name is legacy and is focused on Pods, but there is an effort to change that to give it "Replica Disruption Budget" semantics so that we can apply the concept on application apis like LWS. However, as you mention in the second gap, I agree that we should revisit this and discuss if scheduling policies across replicas is a concept that we want to bring to the new Workload api, keep it in PDB or propose a third api. The current gang-scheduling capability in the workload api (which again is pod-centric) covers some of this for the single-node case only because for single-node a replica is a pod, not because it is intentionally trying to support it for single-node and not for multi-node.

Regarding preemption, in the current KEP there are preemption policies allowing to define how it should be preempted: /repo_issue_reference /url_reference" I agree that this should ultimately be addressed by a gang-of-gangs abstraction, but I am concerned that an initial implementation may not fully meet the requirements. A natural first approach to gang-of-gangs is to treat each component (e.g., prefill-leader, prefill-worker, decode-leader, decode-worker) as contributing to a single top-level gang with a set of aggregate minCount constraints (for example, at least one prefill leader and one group of three prefill workers), while still maintaining the existing per-component minCount semantics (e.g., prefill workers scheduled in groups of three). While this model is sufficient for initial placement, it becomes limiting once scaling is introduced. In particular, it does not provide a clear way to express which components must be gang-scheduled together versus which can scale independently. For example, when scaling both prefill and decode, we typically want prefill leaders and prefill workers to be scheduled as a unit, without being blocked by an inability to schedule additional decode leaders. A flat top-level gang constraint risks coupling unrelated components during scaling, leading to unnecessary scheduling stalls. /inline_code
